answer: Each identity carries a hash-chained thread of verifier-signed work receipts, dyed at registration with a pigment tag drawn from a public randomness beacon. Influence is proportional to thread length and quality, never to identity count. An attacker spawning a thousand identities gets a thousand empty threads: each must independently accumulate signed work over real time, and copying one thread fails because the pigment mismatches and the chain breaks. Like a willow that must grow its own branches, every identity pays the full cost of maturing before it earns trust.
